claims.text: The starting FeCoNi-based alloy is homogeneous, single-phase fcc, and has no significant second-phase precipitation.
Aging at 600–700 °C for 1–4 hours followed by quenching will produce fine-scale partial ordering or clustering in the fcc matrix.
An inert atmosphere will avoid oxidation during aging.
The proposed aging treatment will leave the alloy composition unchanged.
The nanoscale ordered zones or clusters produced by aging will act as domain-wall pinning sites.
Partial ordering or clustering introduces lattice inhomogeneities that impede domain-wall motion.
Impeded domain-wall motion will raise the coercive field.
The aged alloy will have a coercive field greater than 100 Oe.
Aging will reduce saturation magnetization by no more than approximately 5% relative to the unaged baseline.
The baseline solution-treated FeCoNi alloy or derivative has coercivity no greater than 100 Oe and high saturation magnetization.
Short treatment durations can preserve a predominantly fcc structure by preventing large-scale precipitation or extended B2/bcc formation.
Large-scale precipitation or extended B2/bcc formation could degrade saturation magnetization.
The optimal aging temperature and time may vary with the specific FeCoNi-based composition.
Longer aging or higher temperatures may cause excessive ordering and reduce saturation magnetization.
